A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Malenia study. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original segmentation experiments, component ablations, fine-tuning evaluations and lesion-attribute matching results.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds annotation-pipeline ablations, hyperparameter analyses and an incorrect-text-input case study.

M1.justification: The multi-scale mask-attribute alignment, MP-NCE objective, CMKI module and stored-attribute inference procedure remain unchanged. The expanded inference description and clinical knowledge table document the existing procedure; alternative LLMs are evaluated as ablation variants.

E1.justification: The datasets, organs and 12 lesion categories are retained. Appendix F.2 adds a distinct inference scenario with mixed correct/incorrect attribute inputs or exclusively incorrect inputs, illustrated in Figure 8.

E2.justification: V2 adds CT-CLIP (Hamamci et al., 2024) to the fine-tuning comparison in Table 7; CT-GLIP and the existing comparators remain. The main supervised and zero-shot comparator sets are unchanged. Newly discussed LViT and RecLMIS are not evaluated.

E3.justification: New controlled settings compare two LLMs with and without human refinement, sweep 8–28 mask tokens, and increment attribute aspects from one to eight in Table 6 order. Existing training budgets, DSC/NSD metrics, five-fold evaluation and fine-tuning splits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds substantive tests of LLM choice, human annotation, mask-token count and attribute diversity. Appendix F.2 adds an incorrect-input robustness case study. The ambiguous-boundary examples in Figure 7 are retained from v1 Figure 3, rather than new evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five-fold cross-validation and the same practice of reporting ± values for supervised results. V2 adds no seed counts, repeated-run information, confidence intervals or significance tests. Changed ± values in Table 2 are result revisions.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises every method's lung-tumor results: Malenia's DSC changes from 57.84 to 70.96, and the strongest baseline switches from SwinUNETR to nnUNet. V2 also adds CT-CLIP scores and annotation, sensitivity and incorrect-input findings. Table 1's principal zero-shot results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The formal zero-shot formulation, objectives and mathematical reasoning are retained. Equation 1's output index and Equation 5's channel-dimension symbol receive notation corrections; no substantive definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: multi-scale mask-attribute alignment, CMKI and superior segmentation across three datasets and 12 lesion categories. Additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations for the importance of human supplementation and resistance to incorrect text inputs. Its limitations extend beyond the retained cross-domain warning to ambiguous ground-truth boundaries, rare or imbalanced attributes, untested modalities and restricted lesion coverage. Existing blurry-boundary interpretations are largely relocated.

D1.justification: V1 only promises code and references an unspecified clinical knowledge table. V2 supplies a repository address, states code availability, documents disease-attribute lookup entries in Table 11, and promises annotation releases. Appendix B.4 adds private-data provenance, anonymization and GPT-4 API processing details.

R1.justification: V2 adds a focused language-guided segmentation discussion distinguishing LViT and RecLMIS, expands the comparison with ZePT in Appendix H, and cites MaskFormer and MMed-Llama-3-8B. These refine the existing zero-shot positioning without replacing it.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and the section sequence are retained. V2 rewrites inference into four explicit steps, relocates the CMKI case discussion to Appendix F.1, expands appendix organization and limitations prose, and updates publication headers and affiliations.

P2.justification: The combined framework diagram becomes separate training and expanded inference figures. V2 adds two sensitivity plots, an incorrect-input visualization, an annotation-ablation table and the clinical knowledge table. Existing qualitative figures are relocated and renumbered, while Table 7 gains a comparator row.

improvement.justification: The added ablations clarify dependence on expert annotation and support design choices, while inference lookup details, access information and more specific limitations improve transparency. These are useful gains, but incorrect-input robustness rests on one illustrated case, and the substantial lung-score revisions in Table 2 are unexplained. The evidence supports a positive but limited overall improvement.
